title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description: We are building the first AI-native platform for automated product compliance in MedTech . REMATIQ turn hundreds of page of complex regulations (like MDR and FDA guidance) into structured, actionable requirements that plug directly into our customers’ development and quality processes. The result: life‑saving medical devices reach patients faster and safer. About the job As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you build software with and for our customers. Existing customers ask for more than the standard product does. They want further use cases, integrations with their own systems and workflows specific to their organisation. You sit with the customer's team, scope the problem and build the solution end to end. It runs at the customer as custom software or becomes a feature of the REMATIQ web app. This is a software engineering role with customer contact, not a consulting role. You work closely with our AI Deployment Strategists, Product and the platform team. We believe in the value of in-person collaboration and work in a hybrid setup, with the team coming together in our office in the heart of Berlin-Mitte typically four days per week. Build and ship end to end: Design, develop and deploy the solution, including backend services, integrations, AI workflows and the interface it needs. Run what you shipped: Operate it in production, fix what breaks, and be the customer's technical contact for it. Build integrations: Connect REMATIQ to the systems customers already use in their development and quality processes. Move custom work into the product: Build features in the web app and work with the platform team to turn one customer's solution into a product capability. Find the next use case: Spot further use cases while you work with the customer and scope them together with Delivery. Our stack We work in a modern TypeScript‑first monorepo: Core: Node.js 20+, TypeScript 5+, pnpm workspaces, Turborepo. Frontend: React (Vite), Tailwind CSS, and design system. Backend & workflows: Express-based services, with DBOS for durable workflows. Data & storage: PostgreSQL with pgvector, Prisma ORM, Azure Blob Storage. AI & observability: Azure OpenAI, Langfuse, Sentry, plus logging/tracing with tools like Winston and OpenTelemetry. Dev experience: AI‑assisted workflows with Cursor and Claude Code, integrated into our TypeScript‑first monorepo and review process. What you'll bring We are looking for a software engineer who ships production software and is equally at home in a customer's meeting room. You may be a strong fit if you have: Relevant background: 3+ years as a software engineer shipping production software, ideally including forward deployed, solutions engineering or other customer-facing engineering work. Product management or team lead experience: Some experience as a product manager or team lead, where you owned scope, priorities and requirements for what is being built, is a strong plus. Strong TypeScript and Node.js backend experience: You build and operate production services and can contribute to React frontends where needed. Solid database fundamentals: PostgreSQL (ideally), including data modelling, migrations and performance. Integration experience: You have connected a product to enterprise systems through APIs, SSO or data exchange, and have worked within a customer's IT and security constraints. Experience building with LLMs: You have put LLM-driven features into production and know how to make them predictable and reviewable. Strong customer presence: You scope a problem with non-technical stakeholders, explain technical trade-offs clearly, and manage expectations without a project manager next to you. AI-native working style: You use Claude Code or Cursor every day to move faster without compromising reliability. High ownership: You take an ambiguous customer problem to production with limited guidance. Willingness to travel: You work on site at customers when the project needs it. Fluency in English (mandatory). German is a strong plus. We'll be especially excited if you Have worked as a forward deployed or customer-embedded engineer Have built software for a regulated industry such as MedTech or pharma. Have been a founder or a very early engineer at a startup. Why this is a great opportunity Impact in a high-stakes domain – Work on compliance workflows in one of the most regulated industries, where correctness and traceability matter and the outcomes are real. Bring GenAI into production – Build the systems that make LLM-driven features predictable, auditable, and reliable in safety-critical MedTech environments. AI‑agent‑first development – Build in an environment where tools like Cursor and Claude Code are first‑class citizens, helping you explore designs, refactor, and ship faster while you stay in control of quality and reliability. Strong peers – Work with people who care deeply about craft and outcomes, in a high-ownership culture that includes teammates with founder experience. title: Implementation Specialist
description: About Us Hawk is the leading provider of AI-supported anti-money laundering and fraud detection technology. Banks and payment providers globally are using Hawk’s powerful combination of traditional rules and explainable AI to improve the effectiveness of their AML compliance and fraud prevention by identifying more crime while maximizing efficiency by reducing false positives. With our solution, we are playing a vital role in the global fight against Money Laundering, Fraud, or the financing of terrorism. We offer a culture of mutual trust, support and passion – while providing individuals with opportunities to grow professionally and make a difference in the world. Your Mission As an Implementation Specialist at Hawk, your responsibility is to transform customer requirements into a functioning solution that helps them achieve their business objectives around transaction monitoring, customer screening and fraud detection, alongside cutting-edge AI technologies. You start with a signed contract and support the customer until go-live. This includes translating policies, regulatory obligations and risk factors into Hawk's setup, data mapping, workflow configuration, UAT support and ensuring that key project timelines and milestones are met. You support our customers in realising true value by detecting more financial crime, allowing investigators to focus on what matters instead of drowning in false positives, and adopting state-of-the-art AI technologies. Key Responsibilities Requirements and needs assessment: gather and analyse the customer's AML, fraud and screening requirements and advise on best-practice configuration. Configuration: translate policies, screening algorithms, regulatory requirements and risk factors into Hawk's setup, covering rules, screening, customer risk rating and workflows. Data mapping and integration: lead the technical deployment and integration with the customer's systems, via API or batch mechanisms. Testing and go-live: support the customer through testing, UAT and sign-off, troubleshoot issues, and support a successful transition to a production environment. Training and enablement: deliver training to the customer's teams from a functional as well as technical standpoint. Project management: plan and run the implementation from signature to go-live on time and within scope, with documentation and regular stakeholder updates, combining hands-on work with project leadership. Primary contact: be the first point of contact for implementation questions and issues. Collaboration and feedback: work closely with Customer Value Partners for a smooth implementation, and bring actionable customer feedback and gaps to Product, Development and Hawk's GTM organisation. Document every configuration decision and the reasoning behind it, so the setup holds up when the customer's auditor or regulator asks why a rule was set the way it was. Manage each implementation task and the implementation success as an outcome you own, as directed by our Customer Value Partner, resulting in activity completion and a go-live on the dates you committed to. Your Profile 6+ years in implementation consulting or solution consulting, with at least 3 of those years hands-on implementing AML, fraud or screening solutions. Subject matter expertise in AML and compliance. You are familiar with key typologies and patterns, the regulatory expectations behind them, and how monitoring programmes as well as AI get examined. You can confidently stand in front of an MLRO and discuss and defend a rule set. This is a must-have, not a nice-to-have. Hands-on data skills: SQL, APIs, CSV and JSON, and data modelling. You're familiar with standardised payment message formats, including SWIFT MT and ISO 20022, SEPA and card data. Integration literacy. You don't write production code, but you're at home with APIs, JSON payloads, SFTP configurations as well as SSO. Proven track record of taking complex implementations to go-live on time, ideally several in parallel, with banking customers or other financial institutions. Stakeholder alignment. You ensure that internal and external parties both have the information they need, keep them aligned and manage expectations. Able to explain complexity simply. Imagine data models for compliance leads, fraud typologies for data engineers. You do it clearly in writing and in the room, in fluent English. A degree in computer science, information systems, engineering, finance or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Bonus Business-fluent German, for working with our DACH customers. CAMS (or equivalent) certification, or time spent in a second-line compliance or MLRO team. Builds constructive relationships with customers and stays calm and under pressure Builder mentality: works independently and brings structure to ambiguity where no established process exists, taking the initiative to define one. Is a resourceful problem-solver who investigates unknowns and tests system behaviour. Knows when and whom to escalate. Manages expectations proactively. Flags timeline and scope risks early, quantifies them, offers phased options and aligns Sales and Customer Success. Handles product gaps transparently. Clarifies the underlying (regulatory) requirement, offers workarounds with their trade-offs, feeds back to Product and doesn't commit to unconfirmed dates . You use AI tools such as Claude in your daily workflow to speed up mapping, documentation and analysis, and you have opinions about where they help and where they don't. title: Staff Backend Engineer - Search Features & APIs (SABR)
description: About us Launched in 2019, Constructor is an AI-first e-commerce search and discovery platform that helps shoppers find the right products at the right time and enables leading global e-commerce brands to drive meaningful revenue and conversion gains. About the team The SABR team owns the top layer of request processing for product discovery. We own the service that first receives product discovery requests (autocomplete, search, browse & recommendations) & executes the entire business logic that drives product discovery. That service also functions as a gateway to parse incoming user requests, orchestrate calls across the internal services that do the ranking and retrieval, interpret their responses, and assemble the final response the customer sees. We also own the public configuration APIs customers use to control how discovery behaves, and the MCP layer that exposes all of it to AI agents. Our team owns both platform & product components: Because of the positioning of our services, we take part in every architectural decision of our core product offering. At the same time, our goals are heavily influenced by direct customer feedback, because all product discovery-related features are either implemented in or integrated with our services. All of our services are public APIs, so interface design and backward compatibility are a constant part of the job. But most of our attention goes to keeping them fast and up: we serve up to 15k RPS, fan out to many internal services on every request, and are expected to stay available and degrade gracefully when any of them fails or slows down. The work is distributed systems in practice rather than in theory: request orchestration, failure isolation, caching, latency budgets, capacity planning, and the observability to know what is actually happening in production. The team is small enough that engineers own problems end to end, from design through on-call. About you You're a staff-level engineer who wants to own systems, not tickets. You've built high-traffic, low-latency Python services and carried the pager for them. You think in trade-offs: latency versus cost, flexibility versus a public API that customers can't afford to see break, the fix that ships this week versus the architecture that has to last two years. You can lead work that spans several engineers and several quarters, you enjoy mentoring others, and you're fine when a problem shows up half-defined. What you will do Own the technical direction of one or more of our services - architecture, performance, and reliability. Lead design of new systems and public APIs, and the evolution of existing ones as traffic and feature scope grow. Raise the engineering bar through design and code review, and mentor mid and senior engineers into owning bigger scopes. Partner with product, other engineering teams, and solutions/support to shape what we build and to represent search constraints and trade-offs honestly. Take part in on-call for the systems you own, and lead incident response and follow-through when things break. What we are looking for Technical Substantial experience building and operating high-traffic, low-latency backend services in production. Extensive Python knowledge (our primary language). Experience with observability and performance work in live systems. Experience designing and evolving public APIs that external customers depend on. Experience designing & implementing scalable service-oriented architectures. Beyond the code Track record of leading projects that span multiple engineers and quarters. Influence without authority, and willingness to change your position when someone has a better argument. Clear written communication - design docs, RFCs, postmortems. Good judgment about trade-offs and scope. Comfort with ambiguity and loosely defined problems. Ownership that extends past merge, to how the system behaves in production.
